purpose: Bounded realization-stage record for the Navitas–GlobalFoundries US-manufactured Gen 5 GaN route, preserving the distinction between scheduled first shipments and completed delivery or upstream gallium autonomy.

events.geography: Burlington, Vermont, United States; Navitas and GlobalFoundries GaN supply route
events.date_precision: Company announcement date; first shipment and sample schedule is forward-looking
events.denominator: One Gen 5 GaNFast product family and one US 200mm GaN-on-silicon foundry route; quantities, customer count, and delivered units are not reported
events.method: Structured extraction from GlobalFoundries announcement and Navitas public filing describing manufacturing partners and supply-chain structure
events.missingness: Actual September shipment confirmation, volume, customer identity, revenue, wafer yield, upstream gallium source, refined-material contract, recycling share, and end-system deployment are not established
events.exposure: AI infrastructure, performance computing, industrial electrification, and national-security applications require efficient high-power devices; the route also remains dependent on upstream GaN wafer and gallium inputs
events.alternatives_before_action: Navitas could continue using existing Asian and US foundry partners, customers could use other GaN or SiC devices, and systems could defer or redesign power conversion; application-specific substitution is not reported
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Navitas and GlobalFoundries created a US manufacturing route for Gen 5 GaN devices, with September first-wafer shipments, October internal samples, and strategic customer samples targeted before year-end
events.choice_or_response: Navitas developed Gen 5 GaNFast FETs and power ICs for production at GF's Burlington facility; GF provided the US 200mm GaN-on-silicon manufacturing process
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Navitas controls product design and customer sampling; GlobalFoundries controls foundry production and process execution; customers control qualification and adoption
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: A firm-to-foundry partnership creates a domestic downstream supply path for critical power applications; no government remedy or upstream material intervention is claimed in this event
events.immediate_outcome: A dated production schedule and US foundry route are publicly documented; the announcement does not verify that September shipments had already occurred
events.protected_outcome: Potentially improved domestic access to qualified GaN power devices for AI and critical infrastructure applications, with geographic diversification from an entirely foreign production route
events.sacrificed_outcome: Qualification time, customer sampling delay, and continued upstream material and multi-foundry dependence remain; delivered scale and price are unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: Process qualification, yield, sampling, and demand risks are held by the firms and customers; upstream feedstock and supplier risks remain distributed across the broader supply chain
events.later_outcome: First wafers are scheduled for September 2026, internal samples for October, and strategic customer samples before year-end; a September 18, 2026 follow-up search found no later official company notice confirming completed September delivery, so delivered units, customer acceptance, and system deployment remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: The firms frame the route as a trusted US domestic manufacturing source and ecosystem-resilience milestone; no customer, worker, or public assessment is recorded
events.public_or_collective_response: The firms publicly announced the route; no government procurement, alliance coordination, or collective customer commitment is documented here
events.counterexample: A US wafer-fabrication route can coexist with imported epitaxial wafers, substrates, gallium, other foundries, and incomplete customer qualification
events.source_and_uncertainty: GlobalFoundries/Navitas announcement dated September 1, 2026 and Navitas Form 10-K filed February 27, 2026; follow-up official-source search checked September 18, 2026. Shipment and sample dates are company-reported forward-looking milestones, not independently verified delivery

arrows.evidence: The September announcement says the companies announced their long-term partnership in November 2025 and developed Gen 5 devices for production at GF's Burlington facility
arrows.counterexample: The earlier partnership announcement itself projected production later in 2026; schedule is not proof of completed output
arrows.remaining_gap: Pilot lot, yield, qualification, and confirmed production date

arrows.evidence: The announcement schedules first wafers for September, internal samples for October, and strategic customer samples before year-end
arrows.counterexample: Forward-looking schedule does not establish shipment completion or customer receipt
arrows.remaining_gap: Shipment records, sample acceptance, and production volume; a September 18 follow-up found no later official confirmation

arrows.to: AI infrastructure and national-security supply resilience
arrows.evidence: The firms identify AI infrastructure, performance computing, industrial electrification, and critical national-security applications for the product family
arrows.counterexample: Application targeting is not evidence of deployment, reduced system risk, or defense inventory
arrows.remaining_gap: Named customer acceptance, system deployment, procurement, and measured substitution of another supply route

arrows.to: reduced gallium import reliance or geopolitical autonomy
arrows.evidence: Navitas describes multiple qualified suppliers and foundries, including Asia and the US, while neither source identifies gallium feedstock origin or import displacement
arrows.counterexample: Domestic device fabrication may continue to rely on imported epitaxial wafers, substrates, refined gallium, or Asian manufacturing stages
arrows.remaining_gap: Material provenance, recycling share, supplier switch, and measured change in gallium or GaN import exposure

boundary: This ledger records the strongest current downstream realization signal: a scheduled US-manufactured Gen 5 GaN shipment and sampling path. It does not establish completed delivery, customer qualification, end-system deployment, upstream gallium autonomy, or reduced geopolitical leverage.
storage_boundary: No confidential customer, production, or employee data is retained; only public company statements and their forward-looking uncertainty are represented.
